items.title: Alan Raph interviewed by Monk Rowe, Danbury, Connecticut, November 20, 2001

ctx.x: Were you called upon to do much improvising and soloing?

Not a lot. There are two or three records that are floating around that I have a little bit of improvisation on. I did — playing with Mulligan’s band at Birdland, we played opposite Dizzy Gillespie, we played opposite Art Blakey, we played opposite many very good jazz

bands. As a matter of fact it’s funny, I went to school with Wayne Shorter. We both went to NYU. He was a half a year behind me. And I’m playing here with Gerry Mulligan and Wayne is playing with Art Blakey. In fact I got Wayne to write an arrangement for Mulligan’s big band which he did and Gerry played, a thing called “Mama G” is one of the tunes that Gerry played with the band.
